html:
A Genoese soldier who led the defence of the land walls of Constantinople in the siege of 1453.

He came from a noble family of Genoa tied to the island of Chios. In January 1453 he arrived with about 700 soldiers he had raised himself, the largest group of Western fighters in the city. Constantine XI put him in charge of the Theodosian Walls, where the Ottoman guns hit hardest. For weeks his men patched the breaches at night and threw back attacks.

On 29 May, in the final assault, he was badly wounded and carried off to a ship. Seeing their commander leave, many defenders lost heart, and the Ottomans broke in soon after. He died of his wound a few days later, on Chios or at sea. Writers on both sides later argued over whether his leaving decided the fall of the city.
sum: A Genoese soldier who led the defence of the land walls of Constantinople in the siege of 1453.
